summary.text: Peerless illegitimate eldest son of lordly Laomedon, who lay with the fountain-nymph Abarbarea while shepherding his flocks and begat the twin warriors Aesepus and Pedasus — distinct from Bucolus father of the Athenian captain Iasus.

story.text: Euryalus went on after Aesepus and Pedasus, whom on a time the fountain-nymph Abarbarea bare to peerless Bucolion. Bucolion was son of lordly Laomedon, his eldest born, though the mother that bare him was unwed; he while shepherding his flocks had lain with the nymph in love, and she conceived and bare twin sons.
Apollodorus names Bucolion a son of Laomedon by the nymph Calybe — a prose genealogy beside Homer's shepherd-nymph union with Abarbarea.
